Similarly, <term>Moon</term> <note>original: Luna; silver</note> is turned yellow through a solution of <term>Mars</term> <note>original: Mars; iron</note>. Specifically, of that <term>citrination</term> <gloss>the process of turning silver to a golden color</gloss> which is perfected through <term>Vitriol</term> or <term>Copperas</term> <note>original: Vitriolum aut Cuperosam; iron or copper sulfates</note>.

The method for this <term>citrination</term> is as follows. Let a certain quantity of each of these be taken, and let that part of it be <term>sublimed</term> <gloss>vaporized and solidified</gloss> which allows itself to be sublimed, until it is totally sublimed with pressure. After this, let that which was sublimed be sublimed again with the type of fire appropriate to it, so that one part after another is <term>fixed</term> <gloss>made resistant to heat</gloss> from it, until the greater part of it is fixed. Afterwards, let it be managed with the intention of a cautious fire, so that a greater fire can be applied to it for its perfection. After this, let it be dissolved into a most red water, to which nothing is equal. From then on, you must devise a way to allow it entrance into the <term>Lunar body</term> <note>silver</note>. These methods have been sufficiently shown to you, provided you are an exquisite seeker of the work that we have written.

Because we see these things adhere amicably to the depths of <term>Moon</term>, we have therefore considered it certain that these are from the same root, and therefore it happens that they are altered by them. These indeed are all the medicines of the first order which we have brought forward. Nevertheless, many more of their methods can be multiplied, provided the essence of the <term>pigmental</term> <note>original: pigmentalium; coloring or chemical substances</note> things is preserved throughout the variety of methods. Indeed, some have discovered many more medicines, but one of two things must necessarily happen: either it is necessary to create the medicine from these same things or from things having the same nature; or they compose a medicine which is equivalent to that which does not exist, along with its alteration, and which contributes nothing to the world nor to the parts of the world, until the mover in the mobile sublime of nature rests uncorrupted.

<summary>This page details the process of citrination using iron or copper sulfates to tint silver, involving repeated sublimation and fixation to create a red solvent. The author argues that effective alchemical medicines must share a common nature with the metals they are intended to transform.</summary>
<keywords>citrination, silver, iron, vitriol, copperas, sublimation, fixation, lunar body, alchemical medicine</keywords>
